Photomultiplier tubes or photodiodes are critical for converting light signals into electrical signals. Multiple detectors are needed for different optical channels (forward scatter, side scatter, fluorescence).
The hydrodynamic focusing chamber where cells pass single-file through the laser interrogation point. This is the core component where cell analysis occurs.
Includes lenses, mirrors, filters, and beam splitters that direct laser light and collect emitted light. Essential for proper light delivery and collection in all cytometers.
Pumps, tubing, and pressure regulators that control sample flow and sheath fluid. Critical for maintaining proper flow rates and hydrodynamic focusing.

Hardware and software for data collection, analysis, and instrument control. While essential, often consists of standard computing components rather than specialized cytometer parts.
Mechanisms for introducing sample into the flow stream, including sample tubes, injection ports, and associated valves. Important but design varies significantly between manufacturers.
